## Communication backends: Gloo, UCX through commux, an external group (`BACKEND`) {#sec-ch14-backends}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: one `ProcessGroupContext` per process carries every point-to-point message and collective. It is backed by
Gloo, by UCX through the commux library, or by a `torch.distributed` group created outside snapy. **Switch**:
environment `BACKEND` (`ucx`, `gloo`, or the name of an external group's backend); CMake `UCX`. **Default**: `ucx`
on Linux when built with UCX, otherwise `gloo`; always `gloo` on macOS. **Requires**: a `TCPStore` rendezvous
(@sec-ch14-launch) for more than one process. **Order**: n/a. **Defining equation**: none.
:::

| capability | Gloo | UCX (commux) | external group |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA tensors in messages | no: refused | yes, if commux was built with CUDA | no: the non-UCX path refuses them |
| tensors per send or receive | one | a list | one |
| coalesced point-to-point groups | no | yes | no |
| platforms | all; the only one on macOS | Linux builds with `UCX=ON` | any backend name except `ucx` |

: What each backend can carry, read from `ProcessGroupContext::send`, `recv` and `supports_coalescing`.
{#tbl-ch14-backend-matrix}

There is no NCCL path. `BACKEND=nccl` with no external group stops with "Unsupported BACKEND". An external NCCL group
is accepted at registration, but its sends go through the non-UCX branch, which refuses CUDA tensors. That
consequence is read from the code and has not been run.

### Derivation

None: this scheme moves bytes and does not change them.

### Numerical method

`ProcessGroupContext::create` keeps one context per key. For an owned group the key is the backend, the address,
the port, the process rank, the process count and the local rank. A registered external group (non-UCX backend)
is also keyed by its pointer. Contexts are cached through weak pointers, so all blocks of a process share one
(`process_group_key`, [`process_group.cpp:40-91`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L40-L91)).

`_init` does nothing for one process. Otherwise it creates the `TCPStore` (process 0 is its server) and the backend,
then holds the processes at a barrier ([`process_group.cpp:98-142`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L98-L142)). The
three backends differ as follows:

1. **Gloo** (`_init_gloo`) registers a `ProcessGroupGloo` with the default device as the CPU backend of a c10d
   `ProcessGroup` ([`process_group.cpp:236-253`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L236-L253)).
2. **UCX** (`_init_ucx`) creates a `commux::ProcessGroupUCX` on the same store. It sets `COMMUX_COALESCE=1` and
   `COMMUX_GROUP=1` unless they are already set, and on CPU also excludes the CUDA transports from `UCX_TLS`
   ([`process_group_ucx.cpp:22-35`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp#L22-L35)). A build without UCX has a stub
   that throws (`_init_ucx`, [`process_group.cpp:286-291`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L286-L291)).
3. **External**: `set_process_group` stores a group made elsewhere, for example by `torch.distributed`
   (`set_process_group`, [`distributed.cpp:14-16`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/distributed.cpp#L14-L16)). If `BACKEND` is not `ucx` and such a group
   exists, `_init_external` uses it after checking that its backend name equals `BACKEND`. It does not own the
   group, so it never shuts it down, and it takes the device index the group is bound to
   (`_init_external`, [`process_group.cpp:212-234`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L212-L234)).

`send` and `recv` route to UCX when it exists. Otherwise they require every tensor to be on the CPU and the list to
hold one tensor; the error for a longer list names the fix (one message per tensor, #240)
(`ProcessGroupContext::send`, [`process_group.cpp:148-182`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L148-L182)). The exchange therefore sends one message
per variable on every backend (@sec-ch14-msgmatch). Collectives (`allreduce`, `reduce`, `barrier`) block until
done. Coalescing is available only on UCX (`supports_coalescing`, [`process_group.cpp:271-284`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/process_group.cpp#L271-L284)).

The CMake option `UCX` is ON by default on Linux and OFF on macOS; `PNETCDF` follows the same split
([`CMakeLists.txt:12-18`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/CMakeLists.txt#L12-L18)).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_gloo_one_tensor` (macOS builds only) | on two Gloo ranks a one-tensor message arrives; a two-tensor send and receive are refused with "one tensor per message" | exact | `torch::equal`, message text |
| `test_exchange_ucx` (UCX builds) | `test_exchange` on two UCX ranks with three blocks each; local and remote neighbours both seen | value bounds | payloads identify the sender |
| `test_exchange_ucx_cuda` (UCX and CUDA builds) | the same exchange with CUDA tensors; exits 125 (skip) without commux CUDA support or GPUs | value bounds | as above |
| `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam_gloo` (UCX builds) | two Gloo ranks finish with one result line, and it equals the UCX run's line | exact (17 digits) | string compare |
| `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp_gloo` (UCX builds) | the two-rank `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp` passes on Gloo | the test's own | `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp.cpp` |

: Tests of the backends. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch14-backends-tests}

The registrations use `setup_parallel_test` and `add_test` [`tests/CMakeLists.txt:121-185`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L121-L185); the one-tensor check is
`a_message_of_two_tensors_is_refused_with_the_fix`, [`test_gloo_one_tensor.cpp:17-41`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_gloo_one_tensor.cpp#L17-L41), and the Gloo-versus-UCX compare is
`main` in [`run_seam_backends.py:38-60`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/run_seam_backends.py#L38-L60). Their pass status at the pin was not
run for this chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No NCCL path. Multi-GPU exchange needs UCX built with CUDA; Gloo with `DEVICE=cuda` stops at the first send.
- Linux CI runs UCX by default; Gloo is reached on Linux only by the explicit `_gloo` entries above. The maintainer's
  position in #237 and #240 is that Gloo is the macOS backend and is not guaranteed elsewhere.
- `cmake/ucx.cmake` carries site-specific search paths for UCX; they are not part of the method.
:::
